title: A logarithmic-space machine for binary lengths
statement: There exist a positive natural number $A$ and a finite-state machine $M$ over Boolean symbols such that, for every Boolean word $x$, $M$ halts with output the binary expansion of $\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+1$ and uses at most $A(\lfloor\log_2 |x|\rfloor+2)$ work-tape cells. Here the logarithmic expression is understood with the convention that its value is $1$ when $|x|=0$.
hypotheses_covered: There exists a finite-state Boolean machine $M$
For every Boolean word $x$, the machine computes the specified output in some time
The output is the binary expansion of $\operatorname{Nat.log}(2,|x|)+1$
